heroHeadline: Zaidi's Sept 30 Deadline Softens as Militias Float Weapons 'Freeze'; Last US Patriot Batteries Leave Erbil
heroSubtitle: Iraq's disarmament standoff shifted through late August and early September: five Iran-aligned factions — Kataib Hezbollah, Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada and Harakat al-Nujaba among them — proposed (Aug 27) freezing their weapons in private depots for two years rather than surrendering them, a plan Washington and Iraqi lawmakers rejected, even as National Security Advisor Qasim al-Araji quietly recast Sept 30 as only the coalition-withdrawal date, with state control of factional arms now to follow 'gradually.' The PMF Authority Law finalized in late August still awaits a parliamentary floor vote. As the coalition's Sept 30 exit nears, the US pulled its last Patriot and C-RAM batteries from around Erbil (confirmed Sept 8), leaving Iraqi Kurdistan without coalition air-defense cover against Iranian missiles and drones; Baghdad says a national replacement system is at least three years away. Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera (Sept 7) called the withdrawal a 'sovereignty test' Iraq's security forces may not yet be equipped to pass.
